newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary cen. bank stresses caution in rate policy.
newsitem.headline: Hungary cen. bank stresses caution in rate policy.

text.p: The National Bank of Hungary (NBH) will keep its "cautious interest rate policy" and expects an imminent upwards correction in short maturity government securities yields, NBH president Gyorgy Suranyi said.

Suranyi told a news conference that an eighteen-month-old trend of inflation and interest rate decline was welcome and was likely to continue but the central bank has to follow a cautious interest rate policy to protect savings.
"When investments are picking up and their rate in the usage of income grows, increasing household savings are needed," he said. "This has a price, that is why interest rates cannot be let go down."
He added that substantially lower central bank interest rates would jeopardise sustainable economic growth and the long term decline of inflation.
He said he did not see room for credit interest rates, which stand at 20 to 22 percent for the best rated borrowers, to drop when current inflation levels are around 17 to 18 percent.
Suranyi declined to predict how interest rates would move through the year.

But he said a sharp fall in government securities yields in the past 17 days, following NBH interest rate cuts and a government decision on reducing the monthly devaluation rate to one percent from 1.1 percent on August 15, was not justified.
"We believe the market will correct (yields) on the shorter side, while it will freely shape longer yields according to its (inflation) expectations," he said.
He added that the 20.25 percent yield on the NBH's one-year bonds, first issued two weeks ago, was appropriate.

"In the past 10 days we sold several tens of billions of forints worth of the bonds which shows that there is an abundance of liquidity on the market, seeking investment opportunities," he said. "The 20.25 percent yield seems to be satisfactory for these investments."

Analysts and traders expect the one-year NBH bond yield to provide a support for 12-month Treasury bill yields which fell 40 basis points at last week's auction as the market expected the NBH to cut its one-year bond yield.
